Team Name : Solitary Helios 

Solitary Helios is a solo mission building an interactive Martian navigation guide for the NASA Space Apps Challenge. Passionate about space science , Python , AI- driven development. Operating solo for this hackathon, but always down to connect with fellow space enthusiasts!
summary: I built ENYO-1 , an interactive Martian map and navigation web app designed to tackle the complexities of planetary exploration. I developed this tool to bridge the gap between orbital satellite data and surface navigation by giving explorers a seamless way to plan traverses, review reconnaissance imagery, and pinpoint exact coordinates on Mars. It directly addresses the challenge by transforming raw mission data into an intuitive, accessible command center that simplifies route planning and terrain analysis. This is super important because having reliable, precise mapping and navigation tools is vital to keeping future astronauts and rovers safe in unfamiliar, hostile environments.
details:
Building Solitary Helios (ENYO-1) completely solo for the NASA Space Apps Challenge has been an incredible journey. I wanted to tackle a real headache in planetary exploration: how do we bridge the gap between complex orbital satellite data and the actual ground-level reality that astronauts and rovers face?

​Here is how it works and why I built it:

​What it does & How it works: It acts as an interactive Martian surface navigation and reconnaissance command center. By taking complex orbital mapping data and translating it into an intuitive user interface, it lets explorers plan traverses, index surface imagery, and pinpoint precise coordinates in real-time.

​Benefits & Intended Impact: It gives field crews and mission control instant situational awareness, slashing navigation errors in hostile environments. The big goal here is to make future Martian expeditions much safer and more dependable.

​Tech Stack & Tools: I built this using core web technologies like HTML, CSS, and JavaScript, hosted live on Vercel to ensure a smooth, accessible performance.

​Creativity & Team Considerations: As a solo developer ("Solitary Helios"), my biggest challenge was balancing comprehensive navigation features with a clean, high-stakes mission control aesthetic. I focused heavily on user constraints—making sure critical telemetry, suit status, and terrain data are easy to read at a glance so astronauts never get overwhelmed when every second counts!
